_meta.client: collectors.base (robots token RizqJobsBot, paced); no challenge bypass, no header spoofing
_meta.base_py_issue: base.robots_allowed uses urllib.robotparser: (1) first match instead of RFC 9309 longest match, which wrongly disallows NEOM; (2) no '*' wildcard support, which wrongly ALLOWS Talentera's /*/job-search-results/. Recommend a longest-match parser with wildcards. Also: robots.txt on a host with no DNS or a TLS error shows up as 'Disallowed', not as a DNS/TLS error.

fields.note: not fetched. Usual Eightfold PCS fields: positions[].name, .locations[], .t_create, .canonicalPositionUrl (unverified)

sample: robots.txt: User-agent: * | Disallow: / | Allow: /$ | Allow: /careers | Allow: /api/pcsx | Allow: /careerhub/explore/jobs ...
needs_adapter.status: BLOCKER is in our client, not on NEOM's side: RFC 9309 uses longest match, so /careers and /api/pcsx are ALLOWED, but base.robots_allowed uses Python's urllib.robotparser (first match wins) and reads it as disallowed. Fix the robots parser to longest-match with wildcards first, then capture the pcsx call and write an 'eightfold' adapter. Probably the highest-volume giant still missing.
